data_objects.name: subject_physiological_environmental_data
data_objects.meaning: A row-oriented table of physiological and environmental measurements associated with numbered subjects.

variables.name: Skin Resistance
variables.meaning: Skin-resistance measurement recorded for the subject represented by the row.

variables.name: Light
variables.meaning: Light-level measurement recorded with the row.

variables.name: Nr.particles0.3
variables.meaning: Particle-number measurement for the channel labeled 0.3; the channel's size basis and counting convention are not stated in the file.

variables.name: Nr.particles0.5
variables.meaning: Particle-number measurement for the channel labeled 0.5; the channel's size basis and counting convention are not stated in the file.

variables.name: Nr.particles1.0
variables.meaning: Particle-number measurement for the channel labeled 1.0; the channel's size basis and counting convention are not stated in the file.

variables.name: Temperature
variables.meaning: Temperature measurement recorded with the row.

variables.name: Humidity
variables.meaning: Humidity measurement recorded with the row.

variables.name: Pressure
variables.meaning: Pressure measurement recorded with the row.

variables.name: IAQ
variables.meaning: Air-quality-related measurement labeled IAQ; its scale and calculation are not stated in the file.

variables.name: Sound
variables.meaning: Sound-level measurement recorded with the row.

variables.name: Heart Rate
variables.meaning: Heart-rate measurement recorded for the subject represented by the row.

variables.name: Subject
variables.meaning: Integer identifier grouping records by subject; observed group-start rows use identifiers 1 through 14.

variables.name: Relative_Index
variables.meaning: Zero-based sequential index within a subject's contiguous record block in the inspected rows.

structure.description: The CSV contains one header row followed by 33,993 data rows, with 13 fields per inspected record.
Each row combines two subject-related physiological measurements (Skin Resistance and Heart Rate), environmental measurements, a Subject identifier, and Relative_Index.

Records are arranged in contiguous Subject blocks in the inspected portions. Group-start records were observed for Subject values 1 through 14, where Relative_Index resets to 0; sampled following records show it increasing sequentially.

uncertainties: The CSV headers do not provide units for Skin Resistance, Light, particle numbers, Temperature, Humidity, Pressure, IAQ, Sound, or Heart Rate, so all units are left null.
The meanings and units of the particle-channel suffixes 0.3, 0.5, and 1.0, as well as whether the channels are cumulative or size-binned counts, are not specified.
The IAQ scale, derivation, directionality, and interpretation are not specified.
No timestamp or sampling interval is present, so Relative_Index establishes order within observed subject blocks but does not establish elapsed time or cadence.
Subject characteristics, collection protocol, measurement devices, calibration, and experimental conditions are not described by the public CSV itself.
A simple scan found no blank CSV fields, but bounded inspection cannot rule out encoded missing-value sentinels, anomalous rows, or all data-quality issues.
annotation_notes: This semantic map was derived only from the public CSV filename, header, line count, group-start rows, and bounded representative samples from the beginning, middle, and end of the file.
Meanings follow explicit column labels and observed row organization; no unit was inferred solely from numeric ranges.
